name: Georg Stiernhielm
credit: David Klöcker Ehrenstrahl, 17th century · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Georg Stiernhielm (born Göran Olofsson, 1598–1672) was a Swedish civil servant, jurist, mathematician and linguist, ennobled in 1631 under the name Stiernhielm. He served the Swedish crown as a judge and administrator, including in the Baltic provinces, and was a scholar of early Germanic languages.

He is often called the father of Swedish poetry. Working in classical metres, he wrote the first significant Swedish hexameter verse; his allegorical poem Hercules (1658), on the hero's choice between Pleasure and Virtue, is his best-known work.
